## London Crime Data
This example analysis is intended to present some `R` functionality for point pattern analysis. In particular, the `spatstat` package is demonstrated. This is by no means the only, or even the best, package for point pattern analysis. Consult the CRAN [spatial task view](https://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Spatial.html) for additional information.

This analysis roughly follows [this](https://www.r-bloggers.com/introductory-point-pattern-analysis-of-open-crime-data-in-london/) vignette, and we make use of the data prepared by that author. The crime data are from May and June of 2014 (from [UK Police Data](https://data.police.uk/)), and we'll also use a Greater London boundary that has been cut and merged from the Global Administrative Areas dataset [GADM](http://www.gadm.org/).

### Prelims
First, the required packages are loaded, some preliminary tasks are conducted to change variable names and eliminate crime points that occur outside of the Greater London boundary, and a function to draw SD ellipses is created.

```{r prelims, cache=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide', tidy=TRUE}
install.packages("plotrix")
install.packages("MAPCtools")
```

```{r}
library(data.table)
library(sf) # for readOGR
library(spatstat) # for Gest, Fest, and Kest
# library(maptools) # for as.owin function
library(raster) #
library(plotrix) # for plotting circles
library(RColorBrewer) # for nice colors
```


```{r}
path_to_data <- "C:/Users/aasie/Downloads/LondonCrimeData"
```

```{r}
london_crime <- fread(file.path(path_to_data, "londoncrime.csv"))
# the variables names have spaces, so we get rid of that
names(london_crime)
names(london_crime) <- unlist(lapply(names(london_crime), function(x) gsub(" ", ".", x)))
```


```{r}
# some records are missing location, so we eliminate them
london_crime <- london_crime[!is.na(Longitude) | !is.na(Latitude)]
# convert to SpatialPointsDataFrame
coordinates(london_crime) <- ~ Longitude + Latitude
class(london_crime)
```

```{r}
# get the Greater London outline shape

london_shp <- shapefile(file.path(path_to_data, "greater_london/greater_london.shp"))
projection(london_crime) <- projection(london_shp)
```

```{r}
# eliminate points outside of Greater London
tmp <- over(london_crime, london_shp)
names(tmp)
london_crime <- london_crime[!is.na(tmp$OBJECTID_1), ]
```
```{r}
# Gest, Fest, and Kest now require projected coordinates, so we'll just swap to UTM
london_utm_proj4 <- "+proj=utm +zone=30 +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs "
london_shp_utm <- spTransform(london_shp, london_utm_proj4)
london_crime_utm <- spTransform(london_crime, london_utm_proj4)
```


```{r}
# create function to draw standard deviational ellipses
drawSDEllipse <- function(x, y, c=1, ...){
  x_dev <- x - mean(x, na.rm=T)
  y_dev <- y - mean(y, na.rm=T)
  A <- sum(x_dev^2, na.rm=T) - sum(y_dev^2, na.rm=T)
  B <- sqrt(A^2 + 4 * sum(x_dev * y_dev, na.rm=T)^2)
  C <- 2 * sum(x_dev * y_dev, na.rm=T)
  rot_angle <- atan((A + B) / C)
  sde_x <- sqrt(sum((x_dev * cos(rot_angle) - y_dev * sin(rot_angle))^2, na.rm=T) / sum(!is.na(x_dev)))
  sde_y <- sqrt(sum((x_dev * sin(rot_angle) - y_dev * cos(rot_angle))^2, na.rm=T) / sum(!is.na(x_dev)))
  draw.ellipse(x=mean(x, na.rm=T), y=mean(y, na.rm=T), a=c*sde_x, b=c*sde_y, angle=-1 * rot_angle, deg=F, ...)
}
```

### Map all crimes
We may want to map all crimes, determine their geographic mean, and plot standard deviational ellipses at various multiples of SD. Here's how we can do that:

```{r map_all_crime, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.cap="Greater London crimes (all types), May-June 2014 with geographic mean and SD ellipse at three sigma.", tidy=TRUE, dpi=300, fig_height=4}
  point_col <- rgb(matrix(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Purples")[4]) / 255, ncol=3), alpha=0.5)
  plot(london_shp, col=brewer.pal(7, "Greys")[2])
  plot(london_crime, add=T, pch=16, cex=0.5, col=point_col)
  points(mean(coordinates(london_crime)[,1]), mean(coordinates(london_crime)[,2]), pch="*", cex=3)
  drawSDEllipse(coordinates(london_crime)[,1], coordinates(london_crime)[,2], lty=3, lwd=2)
  drawSDEllipse(coordinates(london_crime)[,1], coordinates(london_crime)[,2], c=2, lty=3, lwd=2)
  drawSDEllipse(coordinates(london_crime)[,1], coordinates(london_crime)[,2], c=3, lty=3, lwd=2)
```

We can improve upon that map by plotting each of the crime types with a unique color

```{r map_all_crime_better, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Greater London crimes (all types), May-June 2014.", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
  pal <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral"))
  alphacol <- function(x, alpha=0.4) rgb(matrix(col2rgb(x), ncol=3) / 255, alpha=alpha)
  crime_cols <- unlist(lapply(pal(length(unique(london_crime$Crime.type))), alphacol))
  par(bg="white", mar = c(0,0,0,0))
  plot(london_shp, col=brewer.pal(7, "Greys")[2])
  plot(london_crime, pch=16, cex=0.25, col=crime_cols[as.numeric(as.factor(london_crime$Crime.type))], add=T)
  legend("bottomleft", legend=unique(london_crime$Crime.type), pch=16, col=crime_cols, ncol=1, bg="white", cex=0.65, bty="n")
```

Next, we may wish to create individual maps for each crime type:

```{r map_individual_crimes, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Greater London crimes by type, May-June 2014.", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
# individual maps for each crime type
  pal <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(11, "Spectral"))
  crime_cols <- unlist(lapply(pal(length(unique(london_crime$Crime.type))), alphacol))
  point_col <- rgb(matrix(col2rgb(brewer.pal(5, "Greys")[5]) / 255, ncol=3), alpha=0.3)
  layout(matrix(1:15, nrow=3, byrow=T))
  par(mar=rep(1, 4), oma=rep(1, 4))
  i <- 1
  for(crime_type in unique(london_crime$Crime.type)){
    london_crime_tmp <- london_crime[london_crime$Crime.type == crime_type,]
    plot(london_shp, col=brewer.pal(7, "Greys")[2])
    plot(london_crime_tmp, pch=16, cex=0.5, col=point_col, add=T)
    title(crime_type)
    i <- i + 1
  }
```

### Gest, Fest, and Kest
We may want to analyze the point patterns to assess the degree of clumpiness/dispersion for each crime. We can use functions in the `spatstat` package to compute and plot the `G`, `F`, and `K` functions:

```{r}
london_owin <- st_as_sf(london_shp_utm)

```

```{r crime_type_Gest, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Greater London crimes, May-June 2014: G function", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
  layout(matrix(1:15, nrow=3, byrow=T))
  par(mar=c(3, 4, 1, 1), oma=rep(1, 4))
  i <- 1
  for(crime_type in unique(london_crime$Crime.type)){
    london_crime_tmp <- london_crime_utm[london_crime_utm$Crime.type == crime_type,]
    london_crime_tmp <- remove.duplicates(london_crime_tmp)
    p_tmp <- ppp(x=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,1], y=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,2], window=london_owin)
    plot(Gest(p_tmp), main=crime_type)
    i <- i + 1
  }
```

```{r crime_type_Fest, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Greater London crimes, May-June 2014: F function", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
  layout(matrix(1:15, nrow=3, byrow=T))
  par(mar=c(3, 4, 1, 1), oma=rep(1, 4))
  i <- 1
  for(crime_type in unique(london_crime$Crime.type)){
    london_crime_tmp <- london_crime_utm[london_crime_utm$Crime.type == crime_type,]
    london_crime_tmp <- remove.duplicates(london_crime_tmp)
    p_tmp <- ppp(x=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,1], y=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,2], window=as.owin(london_shp_utm))
    plot(Fest(p_tmp), main=crime_type)
    i <- i + 1
  }
```

```{r crime_type_Kest, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Greater London crimes, May-June 2014: K (Ripley's) function", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
  layout(matrix(1:15, nrow=3, byrow=T))
  par(mar=c(3, 4, 1, 1), oma=rep(1, 4))
  i <- 1
  for(crime_type in unique(london_crime$Crime.type)){
    london_crime_tmp <- london_crime_utm[london_crime_utm$Crime.type == crime_type,]
    london_crime_tmp <- remove.duplicates(london_crime_tmp)
    p_tmp <- ppp(x=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,1], y=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,2], window=as.owin(london_shp_utm))
    plot(Kest(p_tmp), main=crime_type)
    i <- i + 1
  }
```

---

Finally, we can compute the kernel density for two different values of kernel width:

```{r crime_types_kernel_density_default, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Kernel density of Greater London crimes, May-June 2014 with mean bandwidth selection.", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
# plot the kernel density
  Zissou1 = c("#3B9AB2", "#78B7C5", "#EBCC2A", "#E1AF00", "#F21A00")
  pal <- colorRampPalette(Zissou1)
  layout(matrix(1:15, nrow=3, byrow=T))
  par(mar=rep(1, 4), oma=rep(1, 4))
  i <- 1
  for(crime_type in unique(london_crime$Crime.type)){
    london_crime_tmp <- london_crime_utm[london_crime_utm$Crime.type == crime_type,]
    london_crime_tmp <- remove.duplicates(london_crime_tmp)
    p_tmp <- ppp(x=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,1], y=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,2], window=as.owin(london_shp_utm))
    plot(density(p_tmp), col=pal(255), main=crime_type)
    # plot(density(p_tmp, sigma=0.01), col=pal(255), main=crime_type)
    i <- i + 1
  }
```

```{r crime_types_kernel_density_arbitrary, tidy=TRUE, fig.cap="Kernel density of Greater London crimes, May-June 2014 with arbitrary, small bandwidth.", dpi=300, fig_height=4}
# plot the kernel density
  layout(matrix(1:15, nrow=3, byrow=T))
  par(mar=rep(1, 4), oma=rep(1, 4))
  i <- 1
  for(crime_type in unique(london_crime$Crime.type)){
    london_crime_tmp <- london_crime_utm[london_crime_utm$Crime.type == crime_type,]
    london_crime_tmp <- remove.duplicates(london_crime_tmp)
    p_tmp <- ppp(x=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,1], y=coordinates(london_crime_tmp)[,2], window=as.owin(london_shp_utm))
    plot(density(p_tmp, sigma=0.01), col=pal(255), main=crime_type)
    i <- i + 1
  }
```
